### 3.1 Loan Amount

The Loan proceeds shall be disbursed as follows:

**(a) Initial Advance at Closing:** Twelve Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,500,000), to be applied toward the purchase price, closing costs, and funded reserves.

**(b) Renovation Holdback:** Two Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,250,000) (being \$14,750,000 minus \$12,500,000), to be held by Lender and disbursed on a draw basis for renovation costs upon satisfaction of the conditions and procedures described in Sections 6.4 and 8 of this Term Sheet.

The total renovation budget for the Property is Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$3,150,000), as set forth in Section 3.4 below and Exhibit B. Borrower shall be responsible for renovation costs in excess of the Renovation Holdback from Borrower's own funds.

### 3.6 Interest Rate

The Loan shall bear interest at a floating rate equal to Daily SOFR plus two hundred eighty-five basis points (2.85%) per annum. "Daily SOFR" shall mean the Secured Overnight Financing Rate as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or a successor administrator) on the applicable business day, or if such rate is not published on such business day, the rate published on the immediately preceding business day.

**SOFR Floor:** The applicable SOFR rate for purposes of calculating the interest rate on the Loan shall not be less than three percent (3.00%) per annum. In the event that Daily SOFR is less than 3.00%, the interest rate on the Loan shall be calculated using a SOFR rate of 3.00%.

### 3.7 Default Rate

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall bear interest at a rate equal to the otherwise applicable interest rate plus five percent (5.00%) per annum (the "Default Rate"). Interest at the Default Rate shall accrue from the date of the Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or the Loan is repaid in full, whichever first occurs.

### 3.8 Maturity Date

The Loan shall have a term of five (5) years from the date of closing. Based on the anticipated closing date of April 15, 2025, the Maturity Date shall be **April 15, 2030**. The entire outstanding principal balance, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and any other amounts due under the Loan Documents, shall be due and payable on the Maturity Date.

### 3.9 Amortization

The Loan shall be interest-only for the first twenty-four (24) months from the date of closing (the "Interest-Only Period"), commencing on the first Payment Date and ending on or about April 15, 2027. During the Interest-Only Period, monthly payments shall consist solely of accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance.

Thereafter, commencing with the payment due on May 15, 2027, and continuing through the Maturity Date, monthly payments of principal and interest shall be due based on a twenty-five (25) year amortization schedule, calculated using the then-outstanding principal balance and the then-applicable interest rate. The remaining unpaid principal balance, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and any other amounts due, shall be due and payable in full on the Maturity Date.

### 3.10 Payment Date

All payments of principal and interest shall be due and payable monthly, on the fifteenth (15th) day of each calendar month, commencing May 15, 2025.

### 3.11 Late Charge

A late charge equal to five percent (5%) of any monthly installment of principal and/or interest shall be assessed on any payment not received by Lender within ten (10) calendar days of the applicable due date. The late charge is intended to compensate Lender for the additional administrative expense of processing late payments and shall not be deemed a penalty.

## SECTION 4: PREPAYMENT

### 4.1 Lockout Period

The Loan may not be prepaid, in whole or in part, during the first twenty-four (24) months from the date of closing (the "Lockout Period"). No voluntary prepayments of principal shall be permitted during the Lockout Period, and any prepayment made in violation of this restriction shall be subject to a prepayment premium as described in Section 4.2 below.

### 4.2 Yield Maintenance Period

From the expiration of the Lockout Period through the forty-eighth (48th) month from closing (i.e., months 25 through 48), the Loan may be prepaid in whole (but not in part) upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Lender, and upon simultaneous payment of a yield maintenance premium (the "Yield Maintenance Premium") equal to the greater of:

**(a)** one percent (1.00%) of the outstanding principal balance of the Loan as of the date of prepayment; or

**(b)** the present value of the excess of (i) the interest that would have accrued on the prepaid principal amount at the applicable Note rate for the period from the date of prepayment through the end of the forty-eighth (48th) month from closing, over (ii) the interest that would accrue on such prepaid principal amount at the treasury rate plus fifty (50) basis points for such remaining period, discounted to present value at the treasury rate.

The Yield Maintenance Premium, if any, shall be due and payable together with the full prepayment of the outstanding principal balance, all accrued and unpaid interest, and any other amounts due under the Loan Documents. Partial prepayments shall not be permitted during the Yield Maintenance Period.

### 4.3 Open Prepayment Period

During the final twelve (12) months of the Loan term (i.e., months 49 through 60), the Loan may be prepaid in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, without payment of any prepayment premium, penalty, or yield maintenance amount, upon not less than fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Lender.

## SECTION 5: COLLATERAL AND SECURITY

### 5.1 Mortgage and Security Agreement

The Loan shall be secured by a first-priority mortgage lien on the Property (including all three tax parcels and the vacated Anson Lane strip described in Section 2.1), encumbering and covering the following:

(a) the fee simple interest in the Property, including the land, all improvements, and all appurtenances thereto;

(b) all buildings, structures, fixtures, and building systems now or hereafter located on or affixed to the Property, including without limitation all HVAC equipment, elevators, plumbing, electrical systems, and fire protection systems;

(c) all personal property, equipment, furniture, furnishings, and trade fixtures owned by Borrower and used in connection with the operation of the Property;

(d) all deposits, accounts, reserves, and escrows established in connection with the Loan;

(e) all insurance proceeds, condemnation awards, and other payments arising from the damage, destruction, or taking of the Property or any portion thereof;

(f) all permits, licenses, entitlements, approvals, development rights, and governmental authorizations relating to the Property;

(g) all contracts, warranties, guarantees, indemnities, and claims relating to the construction, renovation, operation, or maintenance of the Property, including without limitation Borrower's interest in the renovation contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC; and

(h) all leases, rents, issues, profits, revenues, and other income derived from the Property.

The Mortgage and Security Agreement shall be prepared by Lender's counsel and recorded in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina.

### 5.2 Assignment of Leases and Rents

Borrower shall execute and deliver an absolute assignment of all leases, rents, profits, revenues, and other income from the Property in favor of Lender. The assignment of leases and rents may be included within the Mortgage and Security Agreement or executed as a separate instrument, at the discretion of Lender's counsel. If executed as a separate instrument, it shall be recorded in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina.

### 5.3 UCC Financing Statement

Borrower shall execute and deliver a UCC-1 financing statement to be filed with the South Carolina Secretary of State, covering all personal property collateral, fixtures, and as-extracted collateral (if any) described in the Mortgage and Security Agreement. Continuation statements and amendments shall be filed as necessary to maintain the perfection of Lender's security interest throughout the term of the Loan.

### 5.4 Environmental Indemnity Agreement

Borrower and Guarantor shall execute and deliver a separate environmental indemnity agreement in favor of Lender, in form and substance satisfactory to Lender and Lender's counsel, indemnifying and holding Lender harmless from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from or relating to the presence, release, or threatened release of hazardous substances on, under, or emanating from the Property.

### 5.5 Guaranty

Neil Ashford Graydon ("Guarantor") shall execute and deliver a full recourse personal guaranty in favor of Lender, structured as follows:

**(a) Non-Recourse Carve-Out Guaranty.** The Loan shall be structured as non-recourse to Borrower, except for certain "carve-out" events (commonly referred to as "bad boy" acts) that trigger springing full recourse liability of Guarantor for the entire outstanding indebtedness. Such carve-out events shall include, without limitation: (i) fraud or intentional misrepresentation by Borrower or Guarantor; (ii) misapplication or misappropriation of rents, security deposits, insurance proceeds, or condemnation awards; (iii) voluntary bankruptcy filing by or on behalf of Borrower; (iv) environmental liability arising from the acts or omissions of Borrower, Guarantor, or their agents; and (v) violation of the transfer restrictions set forth in Section 10.3 of this Term Sheet.

**(b) Completion Guaranty.** Guarantor shall unconditionally guarantee the completion of the renovation scope described in Section 8 within the approved renovation budget and by the Substantial Completion Deadline set forth in Section 8.3.

**(c) Payment Guaranty --- Interest Shortfall.** Guarantor shall guarantee payment of any shortfall in debt service payments during the renovation and initial lease-up period, covering the first fourteen (14) months following closing, to the extent that net operating income from the Property is insufficient to cover monthly interest payments during such period.

### 5.6 Title Insurance

Lender shall receive, at Borrower's expense, an ALTA Lender's title insurance policy in the amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000), issued by Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. through Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Title Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective date February 28, 2025), insuring the first-priority lien of the Mortgage and Security Agreement, subject only to those exceptions approved by Lender in writing ("Permitted Exceptions"). Borrower shall also obtain such endorsements as Lender may reasonably require, including without limitation zoning, access, survey, comprehensive, and future advance endorsements.

## SECTION 6: RESERVE AND ESCROW REQUIREMENTS

### 6.1 Tax and Insurance Escrow

Borrower shall make monthly deposits with Lender in an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual real property taxes and casualty and liability insurance premiums for the Property, covering all three tax parcels (Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009). Such deposits shall be held by Lender in escrow and applied by Lender toward the payment of real property taxes and insurance premiums as they become due and payable. Lender shall have the right to adjust the monthly escrow amount periodically based on actual or anticipated tax assessments and insurance premiums.

### 6.2 Capital Replacement Reserve

Borrower shall make monthly deposits with Lender in the amount of Six Hundred Forty-Five Dollars and Eighty-Three Cents (\$645.83) into a capital replacement reserve account, calculated as follows: \$0.25 per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet of gross building area, equaling \$7,750 per year, divided by twelve (12) months. Funds in the capital replacement reserve shall be disbursed to Borrower upon Lender's approval of qualifying capital expenditures, subject to Lender's reasonable review and approval procedures.

### 6.3 Tenant Improvement / Leasing Commission Reserve

Borrower shall deposit at closing the sum of One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000) into a tenant improvement and leasing commission reserve account held by Lender. Upon any draw-down from such reserve, Borrower shall replenish the reserve to the full amount of \$150,000 from Borrower's own funds within thirty (30) days of Lender's written demand. Disbursements from the reserve shall be subject to Lender's prior written approval and shall be used exclusively for tenant improvement costs and leasing commissions incurred in connection with the leasing of vacant space at the Property.

### 6.4 Renovation Reserve (Holdback)

Two Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,250,000) of the total Loan commitment shall be held by Lender as a renovation reserve (the "Renovation Holdback") and disbursed to Borrower on a draw basis for renovation costs incurred at the Property. Disbursements from the Renovation Holdback shall be made upon Lender's receipt of a draw request accompanied by:

(i) a certification from Borrower's architect that the work for which payment is requested has been completed in accordance with the approved plans and specifications;

(ii) partial lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors performing work for which payment is requested; and

(iii) a title endorsement (date-down) from the title insurer confirming no intervening liens or encumbrances on the Property since the date of the Mortgage recording or the most recent date-down endorsement.

Borrower shall be responsible for renovation costs in excess of the Renovation Holdback from Borrower's own funds. Additional conditions and procedures for disbursement of the Renovation Holdback are set forth in Section 8.4 of this Term Sheet.

## SECTION 7: FINANCIAL COVENANTS AND REPORTING

### 7.1 Debt Service Coverage Ratio

Borrower shall maintain a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio ("DSCR") of not less than **1.25x**. DSCR testing shall commence twenty-four (24) months after the date of closing, with the first test date to be the first full calendar quarter ending after the twenty-fourth month following closing (anticipated to be approximately July 15, 2027, for the quarter ending June 30, 2027). Thereafter, DSCR shall be tested on a quarterly basis.

For purposes of this Term Sheet, "DSCR" shall mean Net Operating Income divided by Annual Debt Service. The precise definitions of "Net Operating Income" and "Annual Debt Service" shall be set forth in the Loan Documents, as prepared by Lender's counsel.

### 7.2 Net Worth and Liquidity Covenants

Borrower shall maintain at all times during the term of the Loan:

**(a)** a net worth of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000); and

**(b)** liquid assets (defined as cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities, and unencumbered deposits held at federally insured depository institutions) of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000).

Compliance with the net worth and liquidity covenants shall be tested annually based on the financial statements and certifications delivered pursuant to Section 7.3.

### 7.3 Financial Reporting Requirements

Borrower and Guarantor shall provide the following financial information and reports to Lender:

**(a)** Annual audited financial statements of Borrower, prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP") by an independent certified public accounting firm acceptable to Lender, to be delivered within one hundred twenty (120) days of the end of Borrower's fiscal year;

**(b)** Annual personal financial statement of Guarantor, in form and detail satisfactory to Lender, to be delivered within one hundred twenty (120) days of the end of each calendar year;

**(c)** Quarterly rent rolls for the Property, certified by Borrower as true, correct, and complete, to be delivered within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter;

**(d)** Annual property operating statements for the Property, including a detailed income and expense report and comparison to budget, to be delivered within one hundred twenty (120) days of the end of Borrower's fiscal year; and

**(e)** Copies of all lease agreements and lease modifications executed by Borrower with respect to the Property, to be delivered to Lender within ten (10) business days of execution.

## SECTION 8: RENOVATION / CONSTRUCTION PROVISIONS

### 8.1 General Contractor

The general contractor for the renovation of the Property shall be **Beaufort Builders Group LLC**, South Carolina General Contractor License No. SC-GC-47921. Principal Office: 2200 Boundary Street, Suite 150, Beaufort, South Carolina 29902. The contract sum under the executed construction contract between Borrower and Beaufort Builders Group LLC is Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,850,000), covering hard costs of construction. Borrower shall provide Lender with a complete copy of the executed construction contract and all amendments, change orders, or modifications thereto prior to closing.

### 8.2 Renovation Budget

  **Total Renovation Budget**     **\$3,150,000**

A detailed renovation budget summary is attached hereto as **Exhibit B**.

### 8.3 Substantial Completion Deadline

Renovation of the Property shall be substantially completed within fourteen (14) months from the date of closing. Based on the anticipated closing date of April 15, 2025, the Substantial Completion Deadline shall be **June 15, 2026**. "Substantial completion" shall mean the completion of all renovation work in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, as certified by Borrower's architect, and the issuance of a certificate of occupancy (or equivalent) by the City of Charleston for the renovated portions of the Property.

### 8.4 Draw Procedures

Draws from the Renovation Holdback shall be made no more frequently than once per calendar month. Each draw request submitted by Borrower shall include the following:

**(i)** an AIA G702/G703 Application and Certificate for Payment, certified by Borrower's architect of record, detailing the work completed, amounts previously paid, and the amount currently requested;

**(ii)** lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors performing work in an amount exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000) --- conditional lien waivers for the current draw and unconditional lien waivers for all prior draws;

**(iii)** a title date-down endorsement from the title insurer confirming that no intervening mechanic's liens, materialmen's liens, or other encumbrances have been filed against the Property since the date of the most recent title endorsement; and

**(iv)** evidence of Lender's satisfactory inspection of the work in progress, which inspection may be conducted by a third-party inspector retained by Lender at Borrower's expense.

Lender shall retain ten percent (10%) retainage from each disbursement from the Renovation Holdback until substantial completion of the renovation has been achieved in accordance with Section 8.3. Retainage shall be released upon Lender's receipt of satisfactory evidence of substantial completion, final lien waivers from all contractors and subcontractors, and a final title date-down endorsement. Lender shall have no obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback if an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing under the Loan Documents.

## SECTION 9: INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS

### 9.1 Property Insurance

Borrower shall maintain at all times during the term of the Loan comprehensive all-risk property insurance covering the Property and all improvements thereon, on a replacement cost basis, with an agreed amount endorsement (waiver of coinsurance). The policy shall name Lender as mortgagee and loss payee pursuant to a standard mortgagee clause. Coverage shall include, without limitation, fire, windstorm, hail, explosion, vandalism, malicious mischief, and such other perils as Lender may reasonably require.

### 9.2 Commercial General Liability

Borrower shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum coverage limits of Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per occurrence and Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) in the aggregate. Lender shall be named as an additional insured on such policy. The policy shall include coverage for premises liability, operations liability, products and completed operations, and personal and advertising injury.

### 9.3 Flood Insurance

Borrower shall maintain flood insurance on the Property in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000). The Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X. Notwithstanding that flood insurance may not be required by federal regulation for properties in Zone X, Lender requires flood insurance coverage as a condition of this Loan. The flood insurance policy shall name Lender as mortgagee and loss payee.

### 9.4 Builder's Risk Insurance

During the renovation period (from closing through substantial completion of the renovation), Borrower shall maintain builder's risk insurance in an amount not less than the full renovation budget of Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$3,150,000), covering the Property and the renovation work against all risks of physical loss or damage during the course of construction. Lender shall be named as mortgagee and loss payee on such policy.

### 9.5 Other Insurance

Borrower shall maintain the following additional insurance coverages:

**(a)** Workers' compensation insurance in the amounts required by the laws of the State of South Carolina, covering all employees of Borrower and, to the extent not covered under the general contractor's policies, all persons engaged in the renovation of the Property;

**(b)** Umbrella/excess liability insurance in an amount not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000), providing excess coverage over the commercial general liability, automobile liability, and employers' liability policies; and

### 10.2 No Subordinate Financing

Borrower shall not incur, create, assume, or permit to exist any subordinate lien, mortgage, security interest, encumbrance, or indebtedness secured by the Property or any portion thereof, without the prior written consent of Lender. ### 10.3 Transfer Restrictions

Borrower shall not, without Lender's prior written consent, sell, convey, transfer, assign, pledge, encumber, or otherwise dispose of any interest in the Property. ### 10.4 Compliance with Laws

Borrower shall at all times comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, orders, ordinances, and governmental requirements applicable to the Property and the conduct of Borrower's business, including without limitation all zoning, building, fire, health, safety, and environmental laws and regulations.

### 10.5 Maintenance and Repairs

Borrower shall maintain the Property, including all improvements, fixtures, building systems, and common areas, in good order, condition, and repair, consistent with the standards of comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area. Borrower shall not commit or permit any waste of the Property or any portion thereof.

### 10.6 Leasing Covenant

Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to lease all vacant space at the Property at market rents and on terms consistent with those prevailing for comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area, and on terms reasonably acceptable to Lender. ## SECTION 11: EVENTS OF DEFAULT

### 11.1 Events of Default

Each of the following shall constitute an "Event of Default" under the Loan Documents:

**(a)** Failure by Borrower to make any payment of principal, interest, or any other amount due under the Loan Documents when due, subject to the cure period set forth in Section 11.2;

**(b)** Breach by Borrower of any covenant, agreement, or obligation contained in the Loan Documents or this Term Sheet, continuing beyond the applicable cure period set forth in Section 11.2;

**(c)** Any representation or warranty made by Borrower or Guarantor in connection with the Loan or in any Loan Document that proves to be materially false, misleading, or inaccurate in any material respect when made or deemed made;

**(d)** The filing of a petition in bankruptcy by or against Borrower or Guarantor, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, or custodian for any substantial part of the property or assets of Borrower or Guarantor, or any assignment for the benefit of creditors by Borrower or Guarantor, or any similar insolvency proceeding;

**(e)** A default by Borrower or Guarantor under any other indebtedness for borrowed money in an amount exceeding Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000), individually or in the aggregate, which default is not cured within any applicable cure or grace period;

**(f)** Failure by Borrower to maintain any insurance required under Section 9 of this Term Sheet or the Loan Documents;

**(g)** Violation of the transfer restrictions set forth in Section 10.3;

**(h)** Failure by Borrower to achieve substantial completion of the renovation by the Substantial Completion Deadline set forth in Section 8.3;

**(i)** The DSCR falling below 1.25x for two (2) consecutive calendar quarters following the commencement of DSCR testing as set forth in Section 7.1, without cure;

**(j)** Breach of any SPE covenant set forth in Section 10.1;

**(k)** A material adverse change in the financial condition, business, assets, or operations of Borrower or Guarantor that, in Lender's reasonable judgment, materially impairs the ability of Borrower to perform its obligations under the Loan Documents or of Guarantor to perform its obligations under the Guaranty Agreement; and

**(l)** The occurrence of any other event or condition that constitutes an Event of Default as defined in the Loan Documents.

The following cure periods shall apply to the Events of Default described in Section 11.1:

**(a) Payment Defaults:** Five (5) business days from the date on which payment was due.

**(b) Non-Monetary Defaults** (other than SPE defaults, transfer restriction defaults, and insurance defaults): Thirty (30) calendar days after written notice from Lender to Borrower of such default; provided, however, that if the default is of a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) calendar days and Borrower has commenced and is diligently pursuing the cure thereof, the cure period shall be extended for an additional period not to exceed sixty (60) calendar days (for a total cure period not to exceed ninety (90) calendar days).

**(c) SPE and Transfer Defaults:** No cure period. Any breach of the SPE covenants set forth in Section 10.1 or the transfer restrictions set forth in Section 10.3 shall constitute an immediate Event of Default without notice or opportunity to cure.

# APPRAISAL SUMMARY REPORT

**Summary of Complete Appraisal --- Mixed-Use Retail and Office Property**

**520--534 King Street Charleston, SC 29403**

**Prepared for:** Calverley Heritage Bank 412 Whitaker Street Savannah, GA 31401 Attention: Marcus Prideaux, Senior Vice President -- Commercial Real Estate Lending

This is a Summary Appraisal Report prepared in conformity with the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP). It summarizes the appraiser's analyses, opinions, and conclusions. Supporting documentation is retained in the appraiser's work file. The depth of discussion contained herein is specific to the needs of the client and the intended use stated above. The appraiser is not responsible for unauthorized use of this report.

## 1. Executive Summary

**Property Identification:** 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403; Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009.

**Property Type:** Mixed-use --- ground-floor retail (three bays, 11,400 SF) and upper-floor office (two stories, 19,600 SF); total gross building area of 31,000 SF.

**Land Area:** 0.38 acres (approximately 16,553 SF).

**Zoning:** GB (General Business), City of Charleston.

**Owner of Record:** Hampstead Village Holdings LLC. The property is currently under contract to Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC.

**Borrower / Prospective Purchaser:** Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Item                                                   Amount / Figure
  ------------------------------------------------------ -------------------------------------------
  Purchase Price (per contract)                          \$17,800,000

  Total Renovation Budget (per borrower's pro forma)     \$3,150,000

  Total Project Cost                                     \$20,950,000

  Current Occupancy                                      68% (21,400 SF of 31,000 SF occupied)

  In-Place Annual Rental Revenue                         \$415,100

  **Appraised Value --- As-Is**                          **\$18,200,000**

  **Appraised Value --- As-Stabilized (hypothetical)**   **\$23,500,000**

  Proposed Loan Amount                                   \$14,750,000

  Loan-to-Value (As-Is)                                  \$14,750,000 / \$18,200,000 = **81.04%**

  Loan-to-Value (As-Stabilized)                          \$14,750,000 / \$23,500,000 = **62.77%**

  Loan-to-Cost                                           \$14,750,000 / \$20,950,000 = **70.41%**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Extraordinary Assumptions:** (1) The as-stabilized value assumes completion of the planned \$3,150,000 renovation program within 14 months and lease-up of currently vacant space to 95% occupancy within 24 months from the effective date. (2) No extraordinary assumptions have been made regarding environmental conditions; the property is subject to a recorded land use restriction on Lot 7 (see Section 5).

**Hypothetical Conditions:** The as-stabilized value is based on the hypothetical condition that renovation is complete and the property achieves stabilized occupancy. This is a prospective value estimate as of the anticipated stabilization date, estimated to be Q1 2027.

## 2. Property Description

### 2.1 Site Description

**Location.** The subject property is located in the Upper King Street corridor of Charleston, South Carolina --- a commercially vibrant mixed-use district with strong retail, restaurant, and office demand. The immediate neighborhood is characterized by a mix of adaptive-reuse commercial buildings, boutique retail, creative office tenants, and nationally branded restaurants, all supported by robust pedestrian traffic and tourism.

**Legal Description.** Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina; together with a strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed to the predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443.

**Land Area.** 0.38 acres, approximately 16,553 SF, consisting of three contiguous tax parcels (Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009) plus the vacated Anson Lane right-of-way.

**Shape, Topography, and Frontage.** The assemblage is generally rectangular with level topography and approximately 120 linear feet of frontage on King Street, a major north-south commercial arterial providing direct vehicular and pedestrian access.

**Zoning.** GB (General Business), City of Charleston --- permits retail, office, restaurant, and mixed uses by right. Residential use above the ground floor is permitted. Ground-floor residential use on Lot 7 is restricted by a recorded land use restriction (see Section 5).

**Utilities.** All public utilities are available, including municipal water and sewer, electric service, natural gas, and telecommunications.

**Easements and Encumbrances.** An easement in favor of South Carolina Electric & Gas for underground utility lines, recorded in Deed Book 987 at Page 112, is a standard utility easement that does not materially affect the property's use or value. Additionally, a decorative iron balcony, characteristic of Charleston's historic architectural vernacular, extends approximately 2.5 feet beyond the front building wall over the King Street public right-of-way. The encroachment is reflected as a Schedule B-II exception on the title commitment. The appraiser has treated this as a minor physical consideration that does not materially impair the property's marketability or value, noting that such balcony encroachments are common in Charleston's historic commercial districts and are typically permitted by the City of Charleston under encroachment licenses. However, the existence of the encroachment may require maintenance of a valid encroachment permit, and any city-mandated removal could affect the historic façade. The lender is advised to confirm the status of the encroachment permit in consultation with legal counsel.

**FEMA Flood Zone.** Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard), FEMA Community Panel No. 45019C0418J, effective November 4, 2014. No mandatory flood insurance requirement under federal regulation applies to this property.

### 2.2 Improvements Description

**Year Built / Renovated.** Original structure constructed in 1952; significant renovation completed in 2004.

**Construction.** Masonry and steel frame with brick exterior and stucco detailing; flat roof with a single-ply membrane system.

**Gross Building Area.** 31,000 SF total, configured as follows: Ground Floor --- three retail bays (Bays 1, 2, and 3), each approximately 3,800 SF (11,400 SF total); Upper Floors --- two office stories above grade containing Suite A (9,800 SF) and Suite B (9,800 SF), totaling 19,600 SF. The building is three stories in height.

**Parking.** Limited on-site parking. Tenants and visitors rely on metered street parking and a municipal parking garage located within two blocks.

**Elevator.** One passenger elevator serves all three floors. The elevator has been identified for modernization as part of the renovation budget (\$475,000).

**HVAC.** Central heating and cooling system is nearing the end of its useful life and has been identified for full replacement in the renovation budget (\$1,200,000).

**Overall Condition.** Fair to good. Deferred maintenance is noted in the HVAC system, elevator, and portions of the exterior façade. The borrower's renovation budget of \$3,150,000 addresses these items as follows: HVAC replacement --- \$1,200,000; elevator modernization --- \$475,000; façade restoration (including the decorative iron balcony on the King Street elevation) --- \$625,000; tenant improvement allowances for vacant spaces --- \$550,000; soft costs and contingency --- \$300,000. If city-mandated removal of the encroaching balcony were ever required, additional façade work beyond the current budgeted scope could be necessary.

**ADA Compliance.** Generally compliant. The elevator modernization will bring vertical circulation into conformity with current code requirements.

## 3. Tenant and Lease Summary

### 3.1 Rent Roll and Occupancy

The following table summarizes the property's lease status as of the effective date of value:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Space                Tenant                            SF           Lease Type   Annual Rent     Rent/SF   Lease Expiry   Status
  -------------------- --------------------------------- ------------ ------------ --------------- --------- -------------- --------------
  Bay 1 (Ground Fl.)   Lowcountry Provisions Inc.        3,800        NNN          \$108,300       \$28.50   12/31/2027     Occupied

  Bay 2 (Ground Fl.)   ---                               3,800        ---          ---             ---       ---            Vacant

  Bay 3 (Ground Fl.)   Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC   3,800        Mod. Gross   \$91,200        \$24.00   06/30/2026     Occupied

  **Total**                                              **31,000**                **\$415,100**                            **68% Occ.**

Total occupied area is 21,400 SF (68%); vacant area is 13,600 SF (32%), comprising Bay 2 (3,800 SF) and Suite B (9,800 SF). The weighted average in-place rent for occupied space is \$19.40/SF (blended across retail and office). Lowcountry Provisions is a local specialty grocer with stable operations and consistent foot traffic. Harmon & Wren is a boutique interior design studio. Tidemark Consulting Group is the largest tenant by both area and rental income, providing anchor cash flow through its lease term expiring March 31, 2029.

### 3.2 Lease Analysis and Notable Provisions

**Lowcountry Provisions Inc. (Bay 1).** NNN lease at \$28.50/SF through December 31, 2027. The tenant is responsible for its pro rata share of operating expenses including real estate taxes, insurance, and common area maintenance. The appraiser notes that this lease does not contain an assignment or subletting consent clause; the appraiser does not opine on the legal implications of this omission but notes it is unusual for a lease of this type.

**Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC (Bay 3).** Modified gross lease at \$24.00/SF through June 30, 2026. The near-term expiration of this lease --- approximately 16 months from the effective date of value --- is a leasing risk factor. Additionally, the Harmon & Wren lease includes a right of first refusal ("ROFR") on the adjacent Bay 2, which is currently vacant. The existence of this ROFR may constrain the borrower's ability to lease Bay 2 to a third-party tenant at optimal market terms, as any bona fide third-party offer must first be presented to Harmon & Wren on matching terms. In the appraiser's as-stabilized projections, this ROFR has been factored into the lease-up timeline for Bay 2, adding an estimated 60--90 days to the projected absorption period to account for the ROFR exercise or waiver process. This ROFR should be considered in any lease-up covenant or stabilization timeline imposed by the lender.

**Tidemark Consulting Group LLC (Suite A).** NNN lease at \$22.00/SF through March 31, 2029. This is the longest remaining lease term among all tenants and provides stable, predictable cash flow through the anticipated loan maturity period.

**Bay 2 (Vacant).** 3,800 SF ground-floor retail; subject to the Harmon & Wren ROFR. Market rent is estimated at \$26.00--\$28.00/SF NNN based on comparable ground-floor retail leases on Upper King Street.

**Suite B (Vacant).** 9,800 SF second-floor office. Market rent is estimated at \$20.00--\$23.00/SF NNN based on comparable Class B office leases in the Charleston CBD and Upper King corridor.

## 4. Market Analysis

**Submarket Overview.** Upper King Street is one of Charleston's premier mixed-use corridors, benefiting from strong pedestrian traffic, growing restaurant and retail demand, tourism, population in-migration, and proximity to the College of Charleston and MUSC employment centers.

**Retail Market.** Ground-floor retail vacancy on Upper King Street is approximately 5--8%. Asking rents range from \$24.00 to \$32.00/SF NNN depending on frontage quality and condition. The subject's ground-floor retail rents are within the prevailing market range.

**Office Market.** Charleston CBD and Upper King office vacancy is approximately 12--15%. Class B office asking rents are \$19.00--\$25.00/SF. The subject's office rents are slightly below the top of the range, which may facilitate lease-up of Suite B.

**Comparable Sales (Summary):**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Sale   Address                SF       Sale Date   Price          Price/SF   Occupancy
  ------ ---------------------- -------- ----------- -------------- ---------- -----------
  1      610 King Street        22,000   Oct. 2024   \$13,200,000   \$600      85%

The subject's implied as-is price of \$587/SF (\$18,200,000 ÷ 31,000 SF) is consistent with the comparable range. The as-stabilized price of \$758/SF (\$23,500,000 ÷ 31,000 SF) reflects a premium justified by completed renovation and stabilized occupancy.

**Capitalization Rates.** Market cap rates for comparable mixed-use properties range from 5.75% to 6.50%. The appraiser selected a going-in cap rate of 6.25% for the as-is valuation (reflecting lease-up risk and deferred maintenance) and 5.85% for the as-stabilized valuation (reflecting reduced risk upon stabilization).

## 5. Environmental and Physical Considerations

**Phase I ESA Reference.** Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025.

**Environmental Findings.** No Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs) were identified. One Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) was identified on Lot 7: a historical petroleum release from a former dry-cleaning operation at the adjacent property (518 King Street) resulted in soil contamination migrating to the southwest corner of Lot 7. The contamination was remediated under South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (SCDHEC) oversight and received a "No Further Action" (NFA) letter dated August 12, 2021 (SCDHEC Site ID: SC-29403-0772). A recorded land use restriction (LUR) is associated with the CREC, recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, Charleston County RMC. The LUR (a) prohibits residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1) and (b) requires maintenance of a vapor barrier beneath the slab of Bay 1.

**Appraiser's Treatment.** The appraiser has considered the CREC and associated land use restriction in the valuation. Because Bay 1 is currently leased to Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery --- a commercial use consistent with the LUR --- and because the NFA letter confirms that no further remediation is required, the appraiser has not applied a value reduction for the CREC. However, the LUR runs with the land, and any future conversion of Bay 1's ground floor to residential use would violate the restriction. The appraiser notes that the zoning (GB --- General Business) and highest and best use analysis support continued commercial use, so the restriction does not currently constrain the property's value. The ongoing obligation to maintain the vapor barrier beneath Bay 1 is a compliance requirement that should be addressed in loan documentation.

**Flood Zone.** FEMA Zone X --- minimal flood hazard. No base flood elevation is applicable and no federally mandated flood insurance is required.

**Balcony Encroachment.** As described in Section 2.1, the approximately 2.5-foot decorative iron balcony encroachment over the King Street right-of-way is characterized as a minor physical consideration consistent with Charleston's historic commercial district character. The appraiser does not consider this encroachment to have a measurable adverse impact on the property's market value, given the prevalence of such features in the Charleston market and the general acceptance by the City of Charleston through encroachment permits. However, the appraiser recommends that the lender confirm the existence of a valid encroachment permit or license and evaluate the risk of city-mandated removal in consultation with legal counsel.

## 6. Valuation Analysis

### 6.1 Highest and Best Use

**As Vacant.** Mixed-use commercial development consistent with GB zoning --- retail on the ground floor and office on upper floors. The site's King Street frontage, location, and zoning support this conclusion.

**As Improved.** Continued use as a mixed-use retail and office building. Renovation to address deferred maintenance will maximize value. The CREC/LUR on Lot 7 restricts ground-floor residential conversion but does not impair commercial highest and best use. The current improvements represent a reasonable and appropriate use of the site; renovation is financially feasible and maximizes the property's value.

### 6.2 Income Capitalization Approach --- As-Is Value

**Potential Gross Income (PGI):**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Component                               Calculation             Amount
  --------------------------------------- ----------------------- --------------------
  In-place rent (occupied spaces)         Per rent roll           \$415,100

  Market rent --- Bay 2                   3,800 SF × \$27.00/SF   \$102,600

  Market rent --- Suite B                 9,800 SF × \$21.50/SF   \$210,700

  **Total PGI at Stabilized Occupancy**                           **\$728,400**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Vacancy and Collection Loss (As-Is).** Current physical vacancy stands at 32%. For occupied spaces, a market-based general vacancy and credit loss allowance of 5% has been applied. After adjustment for current vacancy and credit loss, effective gross income reflects the property's present leasing profile.

**Operating Expenses.** For NNN tenants (Lowcountry Provisions and Tidemark Consulting), most operating expenses are passed through to the tenants. For the modified gross tenant (Harmon & Wren), the landlord bears certain expenses. Estimated total landlord operating expenses --- including management fees, structural reserves, and non-recoverable costs --- are approximately \$85,000 to \$95,000 per year at current occupancy.

**As-Is Net Operating Income.** Approximately \$332,000 to \$345,000, reflecting current 68% occupancy and actual in-place lease terms net of landlord expenses.

**Capitalization Rate.** 6.25% direct capitalization, reflecting lease-up risk, deferred maintenance, and below-stabilized occupancy. The appraiser also performed a discounted cash flow analysis incorporating a projected lease-up and renovation schedule over a 10-year holding period, which supported a value conclusion consistent with the direct capitalization result when reconciled with the property's near-term value-add potential and the \$17,800,000 contract purchase price.

**Value Indication --- As-Is.** The appraiser has reconciled the income capitalization approach with the sales comparison approach and cost approach (not detailed in this summary) to arrive at a final as-is value opinion of **\$18,200,000** as of February 14, 2025.

### 6.3 Income Capitalization Approach --- As-Stabilized Value

**Assumptions.** Renovation completed per the \$3,150,000 budget; stabilized occupancy of 95% achieved; Bay 2 leased at approximately \$27.00/SF NNN; Suite B leased at approximately \$21.50/SF NNN. The estimated lease-up period is 18--24 months from the effective date to achieve 95% occupancy.

The appraiser notes that the right of first refusal held by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC on Bay 2 may extend the lease-up period for that space. Any third-party lease offer for Bay 2 must be submitted to Harmon & Wren under matching terms before it can be executed. This ROFR process is estimated to add 60 to 90 days to the Bay 2 absorption timeline. The lender should consider this constraint when establishing lease-up benchmarks or leasing covenants.

**Stabilized Income:**

**Capitalization Rate (As-Stabilized).** 5.85%, reflecting reduced risk upon stabilization, completed renovation, and a stronger occupancy profile.

**Value Indication --- As-Stabilized.** Reconciled to **\$23,500,000**. This value is predicated on the hypothetical condition that renovation is complete and the property achieves 95% stabilized occupancy. It is a prospective value estimate as of the anticipated stabilization date, estimated to be Q1 2027.

The as-is value reflects the property's current condition, including deferred maintenance items (aging HVAC system, elevator requiring modernization, façade in need of restoration) and below-stabilized occupancy. The property benefits from a strong King Street location, a creditworthy anchor tenant (Tidemark Consulting Group LLC), and favorable market fundamentals in the Upper King Street submarket. The spread between the as-is and as-stabilized values (\$5,300,000) represents the value-creation opportunity from the planned renovation and lease-up program. ## 8. Assumptions and Limiting Conditions

1.  The appraiser assumes responsible ownership and competent management of the property.

2.  The legal description and title information were obtained from public records and the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective February 28, 2025). The appraiser assumes title is marketable and insurable.

3.  The appraiser has made no independent survey of the property and relies on the ALTA/NSPS survey dated January 2025 provided by the client.

4.  The appraiser is not an environmental consultant. Environmental information is based on the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment by Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC (Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025). The appraiser assumes the environmental information provided is accurate and complete.

5.  The as-stabilized value is subject to the extraordinary assumption that the \$3,150,000 renovation program will be completed substantially in accordance with the borrower's plans and budget, and that the property will achieve 95% occupancy within the projected timeframe. If this assumption is not realized, the as-stabilized value may differ materially from the opinion stated herein.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Jordan Vickers, Associate, Charleston Office

**FROM:** Catherine \"Kit\" Ashworth, Partner, Real Estate Practice Group Chair

**DATE:** March 18, 2025

**RE: Markup Notes --- Template SC Commercial Mortgage and Security Agreement for Calverley Heritage Bank / Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC Loan (\$14,750,000) --- 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403**

Jordan --- I\'ve reviewed our firm\'s standard South Carolina commercial mortgage template against the executed term sheet, title commitment (PT-2025-04-1178), borrower\'s operating agreement summary, rent roll and lease abstracts, and the Phase I ESA executive summary from Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Below are my section-by-section notes and redline comments for your use in preparing the initial draft. Please address each item and flag anything you cannot resolve for discussion at our Wednesday call with Marcus Prideaux at Calverley Heritage Bank. Target delivery of first draft to the client is April 1, 2025, for a projected closing of April 15, 2025.

**[1. Recitals and Defined Terms]{.underline}**

Customize the template recitals as follows. The borrower\'s full legal name is Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company (SC SOS Filing No. 2024-0011287), with its principal office at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, SC 29401. The lender is Calverley Heritage Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank, with its principal office at 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, GA 31401.

The loan amount is **\$14,750,000**. Note the bifurcated structure --- the initial advance is \$12,500,000 at closing and the renovation holdback is \$2,250,000. Define both **\"Initial Advance\"** and **\"Renovation Holdback\"** separately in the definitions section, and describe the conditions for disbursement of the holdback by cross-reference to the renovation disbursement provisions in the mortgage body.

The recitals should reference each Loan Document by name: the Promissory Note, the Guaranty Agreement (from Neil Ashford Graydon), the Environmental Indemnity Agreement, and the Assignment of Leases and Rents. On that last point --- I prefer incorporating the assignment of rents into the mortgage body rather than executing it as a separate instrument for this deal. That approach reduces recording costs and streamlines enforcement. See my detailed notes below in Section 3.

Define **\"Property\"** broadly to include all three tax parcels (460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009) and the vacated Anson Lane strip. Define **\"Loan Documents\"** to cross-reference the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC (SC License No. SC-GC-47921), the renovation budget, and all reserve agreements. Define **\"Guarantor\"** as Neil Ashford Graydon, individually, of 14 Church Street, Charleston, SC 29401. Define **\"Maturity Date\"** as April 15, 2030.

**[2. Granting Clause and Legal Description]{.underline}**

Use the legal description from the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective date February 28, 2025, underwritten by Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc.): Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, together with the former Anson Lane strip vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the aforesaid RMC Office.

**CRITICAL --- ANSON LANE CHAIN OF TITLE.** Jordan --- the Anson Lane strip was conveyed to the borrower\'s predecessor by quitclaim deed only (Deed Book 1128, Page 443). A quitclaim deed provides no warranties of title whatsoever. We need to verify three things before we can be comfortable with this parcel as mortgaged collateral: (1) that the title commitment from Prestige Title and Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. affirmatively insures fee simple title to the Anson Lane strip without any Schedule B-II exception that carves it out or qualifies the estate as less than fee simple; (2) that the vesting chain from the City of Charleston through the quitclaim deed to the current seller and then to borrower is complete and unbroken, with no gaps in ownership or intervening claims; and (3) whether we should request a specific title endorsement --- an ALTA 9 endorsement or equivalent --- covering this parcel separately to ensure the lender has specific affirmative insurance against loss arising from a title defect in the strip. Review the title commitment Schedule B-II carefully. If the Anson Lane strip is excepted, shown as less than fee simple, or qualified in any way, we have a gap in collateral coverage. This is a non-trivial issue because the strip connects Lots 7 through 9 and its loss could impair vehicular and pedestrian access to the Property and undermine the approved site plan. Flag this for Prestige Title immediately and copy me on any correspondence.

The granting clause should convey a mortgage lien on fee simple title to the Property, together with all improvements now or hereafter erected thereon, all fixtures, building systems, equipment, and appurtenances. Include the standard \"together with\" language for rents, profits, issues, and all other collateral described in the mortgage. Reference all three tax map numbers in the granting clause itself, in addition to the full metes and bounds description in Exhibit A.

Note: The legal description should be set out in **Exhibit A** to the mortgage and referenced in the granting clause by incorporation. We will need the surveyor\'s legal description (metes and bounds) in addition to the plat reference --- confirm with the borrower\'s surveyor that the ALTA/NSPS survey has been ordered and will be delivered in certified form before the closing date.

**[3. Assignment of Leases, Rents, and Profits]{.underline}**

**IMPORTANT --- ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT REQUIRED.** Our template currently uses a collateral assignment of rents, which is the older approach and is insufficient for this deal. South Carolina enacted the Uniform Assignment of Rents Act (S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*), and we need to draft this provision as an **absolute assignment** of all leases, rents, issues, and profits of the Property, not merely a collateral assignment. Under the SC statute, an absolute assignment is effective upon execution and recording; the lender\'s right to collect rents is perfected upon recording in the county land records but enforcement --- meaning actual collection of rents by the lender --- is triggered only by borrower default. Revise the template language throughout to remove any \"collateral\" or \"as additional security\" characterization and replace it with \"absolute and present\" assignment language. The operative provision should state affirmatively that borrower unconditionally and absolutely transfers and assigns to Lender all right, title, and interest in and to all current and future leases, subleases, and occupancy agreements affecting the Property, and all rents, income, revenues, issues, profits, and other sums now or hereafter payable thereunder, without reservation.

**CRITICAL --- LOWCOUNTRY PROVISIONS LEASE --- NO ASSIGNMENT/CONSENT CLAUSE.** I\'ve reviewed the lease abstracts from the rent roll in detail. The Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease (Bay 1, approximately 3,800 SF, \$28.50/SF NNN, lease expiration December 31, 2027) has no assignment or subletting provision whatsoever --- the lease abstract notes \"Assignment/Subletting: No provision.\" This is unusual for a commercial lease and creates a significant wrinkle. Under S.C. Code § 29-3-100 *et seq.*, the assignment of rents is enforceable against a tenant upon notification regardless of what the underlying lease says about assignment, so we are legally covered from a pure enforceability standpoint. However, a tenant whose lease contains no express consent-to-assignment clause could raise practical objections or withhold cooperation at the very moment we need to enforce --- and the last thing the bank wants in a workout is a tenant claiming it didn\'t consent to paying rent to the lender.

Best practice here requires three steps: **(a)** require borrower to represent and warrant in the mortgage that it has the full right and authority to assign all rents under all leases affecting the Property, including specifically and without limitation the Lowcountry Provisions Inc. lease; **(b)** require delivery of a **tenant estoppel certificate** from Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a condition precedent to closing, in which the tenant acknowledges the existence of the mortgage, the assignment of rents to the lender, and agrees to pay rent to the lender upon written notice following a borrower default; and **(c)** include a post-closing covenant requiring borrower to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a lease amendment to the Lowcountry Provisions lease adding a standard assignment-consent provision at the next renewal, extension, or amendment opportunity. Flag this item for Marcus at the bank --- he should know that the Lowcountry Provisions estoppel is critical and should not be waived.

The other two occupied leases are lower-risk on this point but still require estoppels at closing:

> • **Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC** (Bay 3, approximately 3,800 SF, \$24.00/SF modified gross, lease expiration June 30, 2026) --- the lease abstract shows a standard landlord assignment consent clause. Estoppel required at closing but lower risk.
>
> • **Tidemark Consulting Group LLC** (2nd Floor Suite A, approximately 9,800 SF, \$22.00/SF NNN, lease expiration March 31, 2029) --- same, standard consent-to-assignment provision in the lease. Estoppel required at closing.

The mortgage should grant borrower a revocable license to collect rents until the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default. Upon default, lender may collect rents directly upon written notice to tenants without the necessity of obtaining a court order or appointing a receiver, though we should also include the standard provisions for lender\'s right to seek appointment of a receiver in any judicial proceeding to enforce the mortgage.

**[4. Single-Purpose Entity Covenants]{.underline}**

**CRITICAL --- SPE COVENANTS VS. OPERATING AGREEMENT.** The term sheet requires full single-purpose entity covenants for Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC. I\'ve reviewed the redacted summary of the borrower\'s operating agreement provided by borrower\'s counsel, and it does **not** currently contain any of the following provisions, all of which we will need:

**(1) Independent Director/Manager Requirement.** The operating agreement designates Graydon Development Group LLC as the sole managing member with exclusive management authority. There is no provision whatsoever for an independent director or independent manager whose affirmative consent is required before the borrower may file a voluntary bankruptcy petition, consent to an involuntary bankruptcy petition, dissolve, merge, consolidate, or wind up its affairs. We need this provision for bankruptcy remoteness --- without it, Graydon Development Group LLC could unilaterally file the borrower into bankruptcy, which defeats the entire purpose of the SPE structure.

**(2) Separateness Covenants.** The operating agreement does not include standard separateness covenants. We need the borrower to covenant that it shall at all times: maintain separate books and records; maintain separate bank accounts; not commingle its assets with those of any affiliate; hold itself out to the public as a separate legal entity; use its own stationery, invoices, and checks; not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any affiliate; pay its own liabilities from its own assets; maintain arm\'s-length relationships with affiliates; and maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business.

**(3) Restriction to Single Purpose.** The operating agreement\'s purpose clause appears to allow \"any lawful business\" --- a standard boilerplate formulation. We need this narrowed to a single-purpose restriction: the borrower\'s sole purpose is owning, operating, managing, leasing, and financing the Property at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403, and activities incidental thereto.

**(4) Member Consent.** Here is the complication. The borrower has three members with potentially divergent economic and governance interests: **Graydon Development Group LLC** (72% membership interest), **Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP** (18% membership interest), and **Harborline Capital Advisors LLC** (10% membership interest). The SPE covenants --- especially the independent director requirement and the restriction on voluntary bankruptcy filings --- must be binding on all members, not just the managing member. We need written confirmation that Tidewater and Harborline have reviewed the SPE restrictions, understand their implications, and have consented to be bound by them. The operating agreement summary I reviewed does not reflect any such consent.

**ACTION ITEMS:**

> \(a\) Draft the SPE covenants in the mortgage as though the operating agreement already contains compliant provisions --- that is, include representations and warranties that the borrower\'s organizational documents contain SPE provisions satisfying the lender\'s requirements.
>
> \(b\) Separately, prepare a form of **Operating Agreement Amendment** adding the independent director requirement, separateness covenants, single-purpose restriction, and unanimity requirement for bankruptcy filings, dissolution, and merger.
>
> \(c\) Make delivery of the executed Operating Agreement Amendment --- signed by **all three members** (Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC) --- a **condition precedent to closing**.
>
> \(d\) Include a covenant in the mortgage that borrower shall not amend, modify, or waive any SPE provision of its operating agreement without the lender\'s prior written consent in each instance.

One additional note: **Tidewater GP Holdings LLC** is the general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP. Confirm that Tidewater GP Holdings LLC has the authority to bind the fund to the operating agreement amendment. Check the limited partnership agreement or, if that is not available, request a GP authorization certificate or resolution prior to closing.

**[5. Prepayment / Yield Maintenance]{.underline}**

The prepayment structure from the term sheet is as follows: a 24-month absolute lockout period (months 1--24), followed by yield maintenance (months 25--48), followed by open prepayment with no premium (months 49--60, i.e., the final 12 months before the April 15, 2030 Maturity Date).

**CRITICAL --- YIELD MAINTENANCE FORMULA MUST BE PRECISE.** The term sheet describes the prepayment premium as \"yield maintenance (treasury rate + 50 bps spread)\" but does not specify several critical variables, each of which must be defined with precision in the mortgage:

> **(a)** Which U.S. Treasury rate? The Constant Maturity Treasury (CMT) rate? If so, for what tenor --- matched to the remaining term of the loan from the prepayment date to maturity? Matched to the remaining yield maintenance period? Interpolated between two published tenors if no exact match exists?
>
> **(b)** How is the present value of remaining payments calculated? Is the discount rate the Treasury rate alone, or the Treasury rate plus the 50 basis point spread referenced in the term sheet?
>
> **(c)** Is the prepayment premium the greater of the yield maintenance amount or some fixed minimum percentage of the prepaid principal (e.g., 1%), or is it the yield maintenance amount standing alone with no minimum?
>
> **(d)** What happens if the calculated yield maintenance premium is zero or negative --- that is, if Treasury rates have risen sufficiently since origination that there is no present-value differential? Is there a floor of zero, or is there a minimum premium regardless?

**South Carolina enforceability concern.** SC courts have generally enforced yield maintenance premiums in commercial loan transactions as reasonable liquidated damages provisions, but the formula must be specific, mathematically deterministic, and objectively calculable at the time of prepayment. If the formula is ambiguous or requires subjective judgment calls, a court could deem it an unenforceable penalty or refuse to enforce it on grounds of indefiniteness. We dealt with precisely this issue in a prior transaction approximately two years ago, and I do not want a repeat.

**DRAFTING INSTRUCTION.** Insert a precise, self-contained yield maintenance formula in the mortgage substantially as follows:

> *\"The Yield Maintenance Premium shall equal the positive excess, if any, of (A) the present value of all remaining scheduled monthly payments of interest and principal from the prepayment date through the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period (the payment due on or about month 48 following the date of the Note), discounted monthly at a per annum rate equal to the Treasury Rate, over (B) the outstanding principal amount being prepaid. The \"Treasury Rate\" shall mean the yield to maturity, as of the second Business Day preceding the prepayment date, of the United States Treasury security (as reported in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 --- Selected Interest Rates, or any successor publication) having a maturity date closest to, but not exceeding, the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period. If no published maturity exactly matches, interpolate linearly between the two nearest published maturities. In no event shall the Yield Maintenance Premium be less than zero.\"*

A key interpretive question: the 50 basis points referenced in the term sheet. Add the 50 bps to the **loan rate** (not to the Treasury rate) when computing the stream of remaining payments to be discounted --- that is, the remaining payments should be calculated at the Note rate, and the spread over Treasuries reflects the lender\'s bargained-for return. Confirm this interpretation with Marcus before finalizing. The term sheet\'s reference to \"treasury rate + 50 bps spread\" is ambiguous on its face and could reasonably be read either way.

Include the lockout provision as an **absolute prohibition** on voluntary prepayment during months 1 through 24, with no exception other than the application of casualty insurance proceeds or condemnation awards, which should be applied at par without any prepayment premium. Confirm this casualty/condemnation carve-out with the client --- some lenders want a premium even on involuntary prepayments, though that is the minority position.

**[6. Additional Notes --- Other Sections Requiring Attention]{.underline}**

The following sections of the template require customization but are more straightforward. Brief notes on each:

**Security Interest / UCC Collateral. Standard Article 9 language. Ensure we cover all personal property, fixtures (file as a fixture filing in the Charleston County RMC and as a UCC-1 financing statement with the SC Secretary of State), equipment, accounts, general intangibles, insurance proceeds, condemnation proceeds, permits, licenses, contracts (including the GC contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC), and all reserve accounts held by the lender. The UCC-1 should name Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC (EIN: 84-6213750) as debtor and Calverley Heritage Bank as secured party. Confirm the collateral description in the UCC-1 matches the mortgage.**

**Renovation Disbursement Provisions.** The holdback is \$2,250,000 against a total renovation budget of \$3,150,000 --- the term sheet contemplates periodic draws from the holdback upon satisfaction of disbursement conditions. Build in standard draw procedures: written draw request with not less than ten business days\' advance notice, architect\'s certification of percentage completion, unconditional lien waivers from Beaufort Builders Group LLC and all subcontractors for all work covered by prior draws, a title endorsement (no intervening liens since last draw), and 10% retainage until substantial completion. Substantial completion deadline is June 15, 2026. Cross-reference the completion guaranty from Neil Ashford Graydon, which guarantees the borrower\'s obligation to complete the renovation on budget and on schedule.

**Insurance Covenants.** Standard commercial property coverage: all-risk (special form) at full replacement cost, commercial general liability (\$2,000,000 per occurrence / \$5,000,000 aggregate), builder\'s risk during the renovation period, and the reserve/escrow provisions for insurance premiums. The template should be fine here --- just update the coverage amounts and add the builder\'s risk requirement for the construction phase.

**Financial Covenants.** DSCR minimum of 1.25x, tested quarterly on a trailing twelve-month basis, beginning 24 months post-closing (first test date April 15, 2027). Guarantor minimum net worth of not less than \$1,000,000, tested annually. Guarantor minimum liquid assets of not less than \$500,000, tested annually. Audited financial statements of borrower within 120 days of fiscal year end. Quarterly rent rolls within 30 days of each calendar quarter end. These are all specified in the term sheet --- populate the template accordingly.

**Default and Remedies.** Standard default provisions. Ensure we include SC-specific foreclosure language --- South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state with no power of sale. The mortgage should not purport to grant a power of sale. Cross-default to the Note, the Guaranty Agreement, and the Environmental Indemnity Agreement. Default rate of interest: the applicable rate plus 5.00% per annum. Late charge: 5% of any installment of principal or interest not received within 10 calendar days of its due date.

**Governing Law / Recording.** South Carolina law governs. The mortgage will be recorded in the Charleston County Register of Mesne Conveyance. Confirm documentary stamp tax and recording fee calculations with Prestige Title before closing. The mortgage tax in South Carolina is 0.37% of the indebtedness secured --- on \$14,750,000, that is \$54,575.00. Budget accordingly.

**Environmental Covenants.** Use our standard template environmental compliance covenant. The Phase I ESA from Clearfield Environmental Consulting came back clean except for the controlled recognized environmental condition, which has a no-further-action letter on file. The Environmental Indemnity Agreement is a separate document executed by borrower and guarantor and will handle the substantive environmental risk allocation. Standard provisions in the mortgage should suffice.

**[Closing Notes]{.underline}**

Jordan --- let me know if you have questions on any of the foregoing. Prioritize the assignment of rents restructuring (switching from collateral to absolute assignment), the SPE/operating agreement issue (including the form of operating agreement amendment), and the yield maintenance formula. Those are the three most complex drafting tasks and I want to see them handled correctly in the first draft. I want to see a clean initial draft by **March 28** so we have time for internal review before sending to Marcus on April 1.

Also, do not forget to confirm the Anson Lane chain of title with Prestige Title early in the process --- if there is a gap in the title to that strip, we need to know well before we get deep into document drafting and negotiate ourselves into a corner.

One more thought --- coordinate with Marcus on whether the bank\'s loan committee or board has approved any exceptions to standard underwriting guidelines for this loan. The as-is LTV runs a little hot. He\'ll know what I mean.

Kit

Catherine \"Kit\" Ashworth Partner Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP Charleston & Savannah
